ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The magnitude of the magnetic induction intensity around a long straight current-carrying wire is given by $B = \frac{k I}{r}$, where the constant $k > 0$, $I$ is the current intensity, and $r$ is the distance from the wire. Below the horizontal long straight wire MN, a rectangular coil abcd carries a constant current in the counterclockwise direction and is suspended motionless by two lightweight insulated threads. Initially, when no current flows through $MN$, the tension in both threads is $T_{0}$. When a current of intensity $I_{1}$ flows through $MN$, the tension in both threads decreases to $T_{1}$. When the current intensity in $MN$ changes to $I_{2}$, the tension in both threads becomes greater than $T_{0}$.

1. When currents of intensities $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ are passed through $MN$ respectively, what is the ratio of the magnitudes of the Ampere forces $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$ acting on the wire frame?
2. When the current intensity in $MN$ is $I_{3}$, the two thin wires just break. At this instant, the magnitude of the coil's acceleration is $a$. What is the value of $I_{3}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, MN is an upper horizontal long straight wire; the rectangular coil abcd is located below MN, a and b are the two ends of the upper side, and d and c are the two ends of the lower side. The current arrow on the upper side ab of the coil points left, and the current arrow on the lower side dc points right, so the upper and lower horizontal sides are parallel to MN and have different distances to MN; the left and right vertical sides are symmetric. Then reason: The magnitude of the magnetic induction intensity produced by the long straight wire MN at a distance r is B = kI/r. The coil current is constant, so the magnitude of the ampere force on the horizontal side is proportional to the current intensity in MN. Since the distances from the upper and lower horizontal sides to MN are fixed, and the horizontal forces on the vertical sides cancel each other out, the magnitude of the resultant ampere force on the whole wire frame can be written as F = C|I_MN|, where C is a constant. Therefore, when the currents in MN are respectively I1 and I2, the ratio of the magnitudes of the ampere forces is F1/F2 = I1/I2. When there is no MN current, the coil is at rest; if the tension in each thin string is T0, then mg = 2T0. When I1 is passed through, the tensions in the two strings decrease to T1, indicating that the ampere force is upward, and the equilibrium condition is mg = 2T1 + F1, so F1 = 2(T0 - T1). When the current in MN is I3 and the thin strings just break, the magnetic force should be in the downward case; at the instant after breaking, the coil is subject to gravity and a downward ampere force, so ma = mg + F3, namely F3 = m(a - g). From m = 2T0/g, F3 = 2T0(a - g)/g is obtained. Also because F3/F1 = I3/I1, therefore I3 = I1 * [2T0(a - g)/g] / [2(T0 - T1)] = (a - g)T0 I1 / [(T0 - T1)g].

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: MN is a horizontal straight wire above a rectangular coil abcd; the coil current is leftward on the top side ab and rightward on the bottom side dc, so the two horizontal sides are parallel to MN at different distances, while the vertical sides are symmetric. From the text use B = kI/r and the given tension changes. Apply Ampere force F = I_coil L B to the two horizontal sides: because their distances from MN are fixed, the net vertical magnetic force on the whole frame has magnitude proportional to the current in MN, F = C|I_MN|, where C is a fixed positive constant; horizontal forces on the vertical sides cancel. Since I1 makes the tension decrease, its magnetic force is upward; since I2 makes the tension exceed T0, its force is downward, but the magnitudes still satisfy F1/F2 = I1/I2. For the second part, use the no-current equilibrium to get mg = 2T0 if T0 is per thread, or equivalently use total tension notation so the same factor cancels. With current I1, equilibrium gives F1 = 2(T0 - T1). When the threads have just broken for current I3, the current must be in the downward-force sense; after the threads break, ma = mg + F3, so F3 = m(a - g). Substitute m = 2T0/g and F3/F1 = I3/I1 to obtain I3 = ((a - g)T0 I1)/((T0 - T1)g).
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中 MN 是上方一条水平长直导线；矩形线圈 abcd 位于 MN 下方，a、b 是上边两端，d、c 是下边两端。线圈上边 ab 的电流箭头向左，下边 dc 的电流箭头向右，因此上下两条水平边与 MN 平行且到 MN 的距离不同；左右竖直边对称。

再推理：长直导线 MN 在距离 r 处产生的磁感应强度大小为 B = kI/r。线圈电流恒定，所以水平边所受安培力大小与 MN 中电流强度成正比。由于上、下水平边到 MN 的距离固定，且竖直边所受水平力相互抵消，因此整个线框受到的合安培力大小可写成 F = C|I_MN|，其中 C 为常量。所以当 MN 中电流分别为 I1、I2 时，安培力大小之比为 F1/F2 = I1/I2。

无 MN 电流时，线圈静止，若每根细线张力为 T0，则 mg = 2T0。通入 I1 时，两线张力减小为 T1，说明安培力向上，平衡条件为 mg = 2T1 + F1，因此 F1 = 2(T0 - T1)。当 MN 中电流为 I3 且细线刚断时，磁力应为向下的情形；断后瞬间线圈受重力和向下安培力，故 ma = mg + F3，即 F3 = m(a - g)。由 m = 2T0/g，得 F3 = 2T0(a - g)/g。又因为 F3/F1 = I3/I1，所以 I3 = I1 * [2T0(a - g)/g] / [2(T0 - T1)] = (a - g)T0 I1 / [(T0 - T1)g]。

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: a fixed rectangular current loop abcd hangs below the straight wire MN; the current arrows on the upper and lower horizontal sides are opposite, and the whole geometry relative to MN stays unchanged. Instead of calculating the individual segment forces, introduce a signed magnetic-force coefficient C for this particular coil position: because B around MN is proportional to the current in MN and the coil current and distances are fixed, the signed vertical force on the coil is f = C I_MN, with the sign depending on current direction in MN. Calibrate C experimentally from the tension data. With no MN current, the suspension supports the weight, so mg corresponds to the initial total tension, i.e. proportional to T0. With current I1, the support tension drops from T0 to T1, so the upward magnetic force has magnitude proportional to T0 - T1; hence C is fixed by F1/I1 = (T0 - T1)/I1, up to the common factor for one-thread versus total-thread notation. Since the force law is linear in I_MN, the force magnitudes for I1 and I2 immediately satisfy F1/F2 = I1/I2. For I3, the fact that the threads break and then the coil has acceleration magnitude a is interpreted as the magnetic force being downward, so after breaking a = g + F3/m. Thus F3 = m(a - g), and using m from the no-current support condition gives F3 = T0(a - g)/g in total-tension notation. Divide by the calibrated F1 = T0 - T1 and multiply by I1 to get I3 = ((a - g)T0 I1)/((T0 - T1)g).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中上方是一根水平长直导线 MN；其下方悬挂着一个矩形线框 abcd。线框上边 ab 的电流方向由 b 指向 a，下边 dc 的电流方向由 d 指向 c，表明线框电流为逆时针方向。线框相对 MN 的位置固定，上边比下边更靠近 MN。

推理：由于 MN 周围磁感应强度 B = kI/r，而线框电流、形状和各边到 MN 的距离都不变，所以 MN 电流变化时，线框受到的合安培力大小与 MN 中电流大小成正比。可设线框所受竖直磁力的有符号表达式为 f = C I_MN，方向由电流方向决定。

无 MN 电流时，线框静止，悬线拉力平衡重力，因此 mg 与 T0 成正比；若把 T0 理解为两根线总拉力，则 mg = T0。若理解为每根线拉力，则 mg = 2T0，后续比例因子会抵消。

当 MN 中通入 I1 时，拉力由 T0 减小为 T1，说明磁力向上，大小与拉力减少量对应：F1 = T0 - T1（或每根线记法下为 2(T0 - T1)，比例不变）。因此磁力系数满足 F1/I1 = (T0 - T1)/I1。

当 MN 中电流为 I2 时，拉力大于 T0，说明磁力方向向下，但其大小仍与电流大小成正比，所以 F1/F2 = I1/I2。

当 MN 中电流为 I3 且细线刚断后，线框只受重力和向下的磁力，题给加速度大小为 a，因此 a = g + F3/m，即 F3 = m(a - g)。又由无电流时 mg = T0，得 m = T0/g，所以 F3 = T0(a - g)/g。利用磁力与 MN 电流成正比，F3/F1 = I3/I1，因此 I3 = I1·F3/F1 = ((a - g)T0 I1)/((T0 - T1)g)。

raw_record.original_question:
The magnitude of the magnetic induction intensity around a long straight current-carrying wire is given by $B = \frac{k I}{r}$, where the constant $k > 0$, $I$ is the current intensity, and $r$ is the distance from the wire. Below the horizontal long straight wire MN, a rectangular coil abcd carries a constant current in the counterclockwise direction and is suspended motionless by two lightweight insulated threads. Initially, when no current flows through $MN$, the tension in both threads is $T_{0}$. When a current of intensity $I_{1}$ flows through $MN$, the tension in both threads decreases to $T_{1}$. When the current intensity in $MN$ changes to $I_{2}$, the tension in both threads becomes greater than $T_{0}$.

1. When currents of intensities $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ are passed through $MN$ respectively, what is the ratio of the magnitudes of the Ampere forces $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$ acting on the wire frame?
2. When the current intensity in $MN$ is $I_{3}$, the two thin wires just break. At this instant, the magnitude of the coil's acceleration is $a$. What is the value of $I_{3}$?
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, MN is an upper horizontal long straight wire; the rectangular coil abcd is located below MN, a and b are the two ends of the upper side, and d and c are the two ends of the lower side. The current arrow on the upper side ab of the coil points left, and the current arrow on the lower side dc points right, so the upper and lower horizontal sides are parallel to MN and have different distances to MN; the left and right vertical sides are symmetric.

Then reason: The magnitude of the magnetic induction intensity produced by the long straight wire MN at a distance r is B = kI/r. The coil current is constant, so the magnitude of the ampere force on the horizontal side is proportional to the current intensity in MN. Since the distances from the upper and lower horizontal sides to MN are fixed, and the horizontal forces on the vertical sides cancel each other out, the magnitude of the resultant ampere force on the whole wire frame can be written as F = C|I_MN|, where C is a constant. Therefore, when the currents in MN are respectively I1 and I2, the ratio of the magnitudes of the ampere forces is F1/F2 = I1/I2.

When there is no MN current, the coil is at rest; if the tension in each thin string is T0, then mg = 2T0. When I1 is passed through, the tensions in the two strings decrease to T1, indicating that the ampere force is upward, and the equilibrium condition is mg = 2T1 + F1, so F1 = 2(T0 - T1). When the current in MN is I3 and the thin strings just break, the magnetic force should be in the downward case; at the instant after breaking, the coil is subject to gravity and a downward ampere force, so ma = mg + F3, namely F3 = m(a - g). From m = 2T0/g, F3 = 2T0(a - g)/g is obtained. Also because F3/F1 = I3/I1, therefore I3 = I1 * [2T0(a - g)/g] / [2(T0 - T1)] = (a - g)T0 I1 / [(T0 - T1)g].
